What does carpet installation cost in Issaquah, WA?

Figure $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Issaquah — that covers carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and haul-away. Most projects here come in between $2,000 and $4,500; a 1,200 sq ft main floor with a staircase typically lands at $5,500 to $8,500. The carpet grade you pick swings the price more than anything else, and you pick it from full-size samples in your own house.
Does the mobile carpet showroom come to Issaquah?

Yes — the Highlands, Talus, Squak Mountain, Klahanie and Olde Town are all regular stops. The van carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades. We lay the samples on the exact floors and stairs they'd cover, measure the whole house, and leave a written price during the same visit. The appointment is free, and there's no store to drive to.
What does carpet stretching cost in Issaquah?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Issaquah. A power stretcher pulls the ripples, waves and trip hazards out for about a fifth of what replacement costs, so if the pile still stands up and the color still works for you, stretching is usually the smarter spend.
How much does it cost to carpet stairs in an Issaquah home?

Stair carpet installation starts at $18 per step in waterfall or cap-and-band style — worth knowing in a town where three-story Highlands plans stack two full flights. Landings, winders and pie-shaped steps are written into the quote from the start, not added to the bill afterward.
How long will carpet installation take at my Issaquah house?

One day, for most Issaquah homes. Three or four bedrooms plus a staircase is a normal day's work for the crew; a full house with two flights of stairs and heavy furniture can stretch to a second day. Your quote states the schedule in writing.
Will the installers move my furniture?

Yes. Moving beds, dressers, couches and tables is part of most jobs, and everything goes back where it stood. What we ask of you: clear out closets, electronics, breakables and anything personal you'd rather move with your own hands. If a piece is unusually heavy, say so when you book and we plan for it.
Should I restretch my carpet or start over with new?

Restretch when the pile stands up, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room — that's a $99-per-room repair instead of a full project. Go new when traffic lanes are matted flat, seams are pulling apart, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor has outlived professional cleaning. We look first and tell you which side of the line you're on.

All of them — Issaquah Highlands, Talus, Olde Town, Klahanie, Squak Mountain, Montreux, Providence Point, Gilman, North Issaquah, South Cove, Sycamore and Mirrormont, plus nearby Preston, High Point, May Valley and Newcastle. The wider Eastside and the I-90 corridor toward Snoqualmie are in range too.
What's the best carpet for homes with pets?

Solution-dyed nylon with a sealed backing, laid over a moisture-barrier pad. The barrier keeps accidents from soaking into the subfloor — the real source of permanent odor — and solution-dyed fiber tolerates diluted bleach without fading. With dogs coming home muddy from Tiger Mountain and Poo Poo Point trails, that combination earns its keep. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty do I get on the installation?

OC Flooring backs the workmanship with a 1-year warranty, and the carpet itself carries the mill's wear-and-stain warranty — typically 10 to 25 years depending on grade. Both appear in writing on your quote. Note that the mill warranty can hinge on the pad installed under it, which is one reason all three pad grades come along on the visit.
